source_evidence: Unlike traditional mutual funds (or “open-end funds”), they are not required to buy back shares from shareholders. After that, their shares trade on national securities exchanges at market prices. The market price may be greater or less than the market value of the fund’s underlying investments.
answer: A publicly traded closed-end fund pools investors’ money and invests it in assets such as stocks or bonds. Unlike a traditional mutual fund, it is not required to buy back its shares from shareholders. After its public offering, its shares trade on national securities exchanges, and their market price can be higher or lower than the market value of the fund’s underlying investments.
